note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on any of these courts. Every sentence below is drawn from a source listed in this file: Raleigh Parks' pickleball page, each park's own page on raleighnc.gov, the department's guidelines and status alerts, and its GIS inventories. Where a source is silent the note says so, and where two city sources disagree the disagreement is written into the venue's page.

slots.description: Baileywick Park is the only place in this directory's Raleigh set where you can play pickleball under a roof, and the only one where the city's two inventories disagree about how much pickleball there is. The park's page lists three hard courts (Court A covered, Court B covered centre, Court C uncovered), and the weekly schedule puts pickleball on Courts A and B. Raleigh Parks' pickleball page says six pickleball courts; the GIS Athletic Courts layer, with polygons for A and B and none for C, adds up to four. Six is published here because it reconciles with the citywide total of 44, and the venue is flagged for a re-check. The courts are lit and shared with basketball open play, a youth basketball league and futsal.
slots.getting_there: Baileywick is in the far north of the city at 9501 Baileywick Road, and its page names a parking lot at that address. A paved walking trail runs from the Baileywick Road entrance, loops behind the playground and comes out at the parking lot. There is a restroom facility on site. The .6-mile Baileywick Greenway Trail connects Strickland Road to Baileywick Road through the park.
slots.what_to_expect: Pickleball has Courts A and B on Monday to Friday from noon to 4 p.m., Saturday from 3 to 9 p.m. and Sunday from 7 a.m. to 2 p.m. Outside those windows the courts belong to basketball or futsal. Walk-up play is first-come, first-served, but walk-up use is not allowed on courts scheduled for a league or programmed activity, and the scheduled activity has priority. On 24 August 2026 the department posted that Baileywick Park Pavilion-Court A is closed for repairs, with no reopening date given. Nothing published says whether nets are provided, and nothing published gives a surface.

faqs.q: Are the pickleball courts at Baileywick Park covered?
faqs.a: Partly. The park page lists Court A as covered and Court B as covered centre, and pickleball is scheduled on Courts A and B. They still count as outdoor courts, because a roof is not the same as being indoors. Court C, which pickleball does not normally use, is uncovered.

faqs.q: Is Baileywick Park open right now?
faqs.a: Court A was closed for repairs as of 24 August 2026 with no reopening date published. Pickleball here runs on Courts A and B, so that is half the pickleball surface. Check the park's page before travelling.

slots.description: Carolina Pines is a neighbourhood park in south Raleigh with a community centre attached, and its pickleball is painted onto its tennis courts. Raleigh Parks lists four pickleball courts here and marks them lit, and its note for this location says you need to bring or borrow a net. The park's own page records three tennis courts with push-button lighting from dusk to 10 p.m. and no backboards. The GIS Athletic Courts layer records three pickleball courts against the pickleball page's four; four is published here because it reconciles with the citywide total of 44, and the venue is flagged for a re-check. The park also holds two unlit volleyball courts, three lit ball fields and a new accessible playground.
slots.getting_there: The park is at 2305 Lake Wheeler Road, postcode 27603, south-west of downtown. Raleigh Parks publishes no parking guidance for these courts. A restroom is recorded in the city's park amenities inventory. The community centre keeps its own hours, Monday to Friday 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., Saturday 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. and Sunday 1 to 6 p.m., which are not court hours.
slots.what_to_expect: Bring a net, because the city tells you to. The pickleball lines sit on tennis courts, so the courts can be in use for tennis when you arrive. The lighting is push-button rather than on a timer, according to the park page, and runs to 10 p.m. Raleigh Parks' guidelines apply: sign in or place a paddle, games to 11 and win by 2, and all four players come off at the end of each game. No source states a surface material for these courts, and none states a fee either way.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net to Carolina Pines Park?
faqs.a: Yes. Raleigh Parks' note for this location says you need to bring or borrow a net. Southgate Park is the only other Raleigh location where the department says so.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Carolina Pines have?
faqs.a: Raleigh Parks says four and its GIS court inventory says three. The department's four is published here, because its per-location figures add up to the citywide total of 44 it states, and the venue is flagged for a re-check.

slots.description: Fred Fletcher Park sits just north-west of downtown Raleigh on the former campus of the Methodist Home for Children, bought by the City in 1982. For pickleball it has two courts, lines painted on the park's tennis courts, and no lights. Raleigh Parks marks this location No in the Lights column of its pickleball table, and the park's own page records its tennis courts as having no lights and no backboard. It is one of two daylight-only pickleball locations in the city, with Southgate Park. The rest of the park holds an outdoor basketball court, a picnic shelter for 36 to 60, a softball field, a multipurpose field of 300 by 195 feet, a playground for ages 2 to 12 on sand, a water garden and wetland, and walking paths.
slots.getting_there: The park's page gives the address as 820 Clay Street and 805 Washington Street, postcode 27605, with entrances off St. Mary's Street and Glenwood Avenue; the city's park amenities inventory records 805 Washington Street. 820 Clay Street is published here with the other as an alternative. Raleigh Parks' pickleball table lists this park at "514 Method Road", which is Method Community Park's address in the row below (a duplicated cell, not a second location). No parking guidance is published, and no restroom is recorded.
slots.what_to_expect: Daylight play only, on tennis courts. With no floodlights, the usable window is short in winter. Nothing published says whether nets are provided, so bring one. Nothing published gives a surface material or its condition. The hard courts share the site with basketball, a softball field, a large multipurpose field and a playground. Raleigh Parks' sign-up guidelines apply: place a paddle or sign in, games to 11 and win by 2, and all four come off at the end of each game.

faqs.q: Does Fred Fletcher Park have lights?
faqs.a: No. Raleigh Parks marks the location as unlit in its pickleball table, and the park's own page records its tennis courts as having no lights. It is one of two daylight-only pickleball locations in the city.

faqs.q: What is the address of Fred Fletcher Park?
faqs.a: 820 Clay Street or 805 Washington Street, Raleigh 27605, with entrances off St. Mary's Street and Glenwood Avenue. Ignore the "514 Method Road" against this park in the city's pickleball table; that is Method Community Park's address, duplicated from the row below.

slots.description: Jaycee Park is a community park on Wade Avenue, west of downtown, and its pickleball is two courts of lines on the park's tennis courts. Raleigh Parks marks the location as lit, and the city's lit courts run on a timer to 10 p.m. The park is best known locally for its dog run, which has an accessible sidewalk to the parking lot on Wade Avenue, with benches, trash cans and a dog waste station inside. A community centre shares the site and keeps its own hours. Pickleball is one of several things happening here, and the two courts are shared with tennis.
slots.getting_there: 2405 Wade Avenue, postcode 27607. The park page notes a parking lot on Wade Avenue and says ample parking is provided on both sides of the dog run, though it is describing the route to the dog run rather than to the courts. No capacity, time limit or permit information is published. A restroom is recorded in the city's park amenities inventory.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts, lit, shared with tennis. Nothing published states whether nets are provided here, so bring one. Nothing published gives the surface material. Raleigh Parks' rotation guidelines apply: each player signs in or places a paddle, games are singles or doubles to 11 and win by 2, and at the end of each game all four players leave the court so the next four can play. Groups wanting to stay together are asked to skip to the next fully open quadrant.

faqs.q: Can I play at Jaycee Park in the evening?
faqs.a: Raleigh Parks marks this location as lit and says its outdoor court lighting runs on a timer until 10 p.m. Nothing published states what time the lights come on beyond dusk, or whether the timer changes with the season.

faqs.q: Are the courts at Jaycee Park pickleball-only?
faqs.a: No. The department lists them as tennis courts with pickleball lines, so tennis players may have them when you arrive.

slots.description: Method Community Park holds six permanent pickleball courts, one of three locations in the city where the courts are built for pickleball rather than painted onto something else. Both city inventories agree on the number. The park's page states "6 courts", "Lighting on timer from dusk to 10 p.m." and "Has backboards", and asks players to follow posted rules on rotating courts. Raleigh Parks marks the location "Drop in only, no reservations", so the courts cannot be booked out ahead of you. The park shares its address with the Method Road Community Centre, one of thirteen sites running the city's indoor pickleball programme; the gym can be rented for what the city describes as three pickle courts and one volleyball court at $85 an hour.
slots.getting_there: 514 Method Road, postcode 27607, west of downtown near the NC State campus. Raleigh Parks publishes no parking guidance for the courts, and no restroom is recorded for the park in the city's amenities inventory, though the community centre on the same site keeps public hours. The city's pickleball table also lists Fred Fletcher Park at this address by mistake; that is a different park about two miles away.
slots.what_to_expect: Six permanent courts with backboards, lit on a timer from dusk to 10 p.m., and no reservations. Raleigh Parks' sign-up procedure applies: players sign in or place a paddle, games are singles or doubles to 11 points and win by 2, and at the end of every game all four players leave the court and the next four go on. That rotation makes a permanent-court site workable for a single player. The city does not publish a surface material, whether nets are provided outdoors, or any fee. The $3 session and $15 four-month pass are for the indoor programme in the gym.

faqs.q: Can I reserve a court at Method Community Park?
faqs.a: No. Raleigh Parks marks this location "Drop in only, no reservations". Other Raleigh locations take bookings through the department's pickleball court reservation form, but this is not one of them.

faqs.q: Is there indoor pickleball at Method Road?
faqs.a: The community centre on this site is one of thirteen running Raleigh's indoor open-play programme, at $3 a session or $15 for a four-month pass, with nets and balls provided. The city does not publish how many courts the gym holds for open play, so it is not verified as a venue here.

slots.description: North Hills Park has six permanent pickleball courts in north Raleigh. With Method Community Park it is one of two locations the city marks "Drop in only, no reservations", so the courts cannot be booked out ahead of you. The city's pickleball page and its GIS court inventory agree on the count, and so does the commercial dataset this directory started from, which is a rarer alignment than it ought to be. The park page has a pickleball section of its own, gives pickleball@raleighnc.gov for questions, and states that court reservations are not offered during open play. The courts are lit, but Raleigh Parks began a lighting upgrade on 24 August 2026 and closed the courts. Daytime play reopened on Wednesday 2 September, with 8 September targeted for completion and night play unavailable until the work finishes.
slots.getting_there: 100 Chowan Circle, postcode 27609, in the North Hills area north of the Beltline. No parking guidance is published for the courts. A restroom is recorded at this park in the city's amenities inventory. Do not confuse this park with the private North Hills Club nearby, which is a different venue and is not verified here.
slots.what_to_expect: Six permanent courts, drop-in only, and once the upgrade has finished, lights on a timer to 10 p.m. The department's sign-up rules apply: sign in or place a paddle, games to 11 and win by 2, and all four players come off at the end of each game so the next four can go on. The rotation is the queueing system, so a group of four cannot hold a court indefinitely. Not published: the surface material, whether nets are provided outdoors, or any fee. Before an evening trip, check the park's status page; the lighting work was still listed as incomplete on 3 September 2026.

faqs.q: Are North Hills Park's pickleball courts open?
faqs.a: Daytime play reopened on 2 September 2026 after a lighting upgrade that began on 24 August. Night play was still closed on 3 September, with Raleigh Parks targeting 8 September for completion. Check the park's page before an evening visit.

faqs.q: Can I book a court at North Hills Park?
faqs.a: No. Raleigh Parks marks the location "Drop in only, no reservations", and the park's own page states that court reservations are not offered during open play.

slots.description: Powell Drive Park is a neighbourhood park in south-west Raleigh with two pickleball courts, lines painted on its tennis courts, and lights. It is one of six Raleigh locations where pickleball shares a tennis surface, and one of nine that are lit. Both the department's pickleball page and its GIS court inventory record two courts here. The park page describes an outdoor basketball court with a concrete surface, but publishes no surface for the tennis courts the pickleball lines sit on, so none is stated here. The city publishes very little else about the park.
slots.getting_there: 740 Powell Drive, postcode 27606. Raleigh Parks publishes no parking guidance for this park, and no restroom is recorded here in the city's park amenities inventory. The nearest verified restrooms in this set are at Carolina Pines Park and Jaycee Park.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts of pickleball lines over tennis, lit to 10 p.m. on the city's timer. A tennis player has as much claim on the surface as you do, and with two courts a queue builds quickly. Raleigh Parks' guidelines apply: sign in or place your paddle, games singles or doubles to 11 and win by 2, and all four players off at the end of each game. Groups who want to stay together are asked to skip to the next fully open quadrant. Nothing published says whether nets are provided, so take one if you can. No fee is published for the outdoor courts.

faqs.q: Are there lights at Powell Drive Park?
faqs.a: Yes. Raleigh Parks marks the location as lit in its pickleball table and its GIS court inventory records lighting on the pickleball courts here. The lights run on a timer until 10 p.m.

faqs.q: Is there a restroom at Powell Drive Park?
faqs.a: None is recorded in the city's park amenities inventory for this park. That inventory records restrooms at five of the eleven Raleigh pickleball locations, so it is published as unverified rather than as a confirmed absence.

slots.description: Roberts Park is in south-east Raleigh, close to the centre on East Martin Street, with two lit pickleball courts painted onto its tennis courts. The department's pickleball page and its GIS court inventory agree on the count. It is one of five locations in the Raleigh set where the city's park amenities inventory records a restroom, and it is a central option in a city whose largest pickleball sites are all some way out. The park also has an outdoor basketball court. The pickleball lines share a surface with tennis. Nothing published gives the surface material or its condition, and nothing published states a fee for the outdoor courts.
slots.getting_there: 1300 E. Martin Street, postcode 27610. No parking guidance is published for this park. A restroom is recorded on site in the city's park amenities inventory. A community centre shares the site and keeps its own published hours, which are not court hours.
slots.what_to_expect: Two lit courts, shared with tennis. The lights run on a timer to 10 p.m. Raleigh Parks' rotation guidelines apply: sign in or place your paddle in a quadrant of four, games to 11 and win by 2, and all four come off at the end of each game so the next four can go on. Groups who want to stay together are asked to skip to the next fully open quadrant. With two courts at a central park, that queue decides how long you wait. The city does not publish whether nets are provided, so bring one. The $3 and $15 prices Raleigh advertises are for the indoor community-centre programme, not these courts.

faqs.q: Is there a restroom at Roberts Park?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's park amenities inventory records a restroom here, which is true at only five of the eleven Raleigh pickleball locations.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to play at Roberts Park?
faqs.a: No fee is published for the outdoor courts, and no source states that they are free either, so cost is not verified. The prices Raleigh Parks does publish ($3 a session, $15 for four months) are for indoor open play at its community centres.

slots.description: Sanderford Road Park is the largest pickleball site in Raleigh and the largest in this directory's Wake County coverage: ten permanent courts, lit, on a single site in the south-east of the city. That is nearly a quarter of the city's 44 outdoor courts in one park. Raleigh Parks' pickleball page, the department's GIS court inventory and independent pickleball listings all give ten. The department marks the location as permanent courts, and unlike Method and North Hills it does not mark it drop-in only; the park's own page states that court reservations are available here, so some of the ten may be booked when you arrive. The park also holds an outdoor basketball court with four hoops on a concrete surface. If you are new to the city and want the best odds of getting a game, this is the site to try first.
slots.getting_there: 2623 Sanderford Road, postcode 27610, in south-east Raleigh. Both of the city's records give that address; some third-party listings show 2823, which does not match either city source. Raleigh Parks publishes no parking guidance for the courts, and no restroom is recorded for this park in the city's amenities inventory.
slots.what_to_expect: Ten permanent courts is enough that the sign-up system does real work. Players sign in or place a paddle in a quadrant of four, games are to 11 points and win by 2, and at the end of each game all four players leave the court and the next four go on. Because reservations are available here, check the department's monthly pickleball calendar before travelling. The lights run on the city's timer to 10 p.m. No surface material is published, no fee is published, and the city does not state whether nets are provided, so take one.

faqs.q: Can I reserve a court at Sanderford Road Park?
faqs.a: The park's own page says court reservations are available here, and Raleigh Parks publishes a pickleball court reservation form. Method Community Park and North Hills Park, by contrast, are marked drop-in only. Check the department's monthly pickleball calendar before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there a restroom at Sanderford Road Park?
faqs.a: None is recorded for this park in the city's park amenities inventory. That is published as unverified rather than as a confirmed absence, but plan for it at a ten-court site where you may be there a while.

slots.description: Southgate Park is the one Raleigh location where the city publishes a surface. Its two pickleball courts are lines painted on basketball courts rather than tennis courts, the only location in the city where that is true, and the GIS court inventory records the surface as asphalt, the single populated surface value across every pickleball court polygon in all eleven Raleigh parks. It is also one of two unlit locations, with Fred Fletcher Park, so play here is a daylight proposition. Raleigh Parks' note for this location says you need to bring your own net.
slots.getting_there: 1801 Proctor Street, postcode 27610, in south-east Raleigh. The department's pickleball page and the park's own page give the street as Proctor Street, while the city's GIS park amenities inventory records it as Proctor Rd; the two park-facing pages are followed here. No parking guidance is published, and no restroom is recorded for this park in the city's amenities inventory.
slots.what_to_expect: Bring a net, and come in daylight. Raleigh Parks says to bring your own net here, and marks the location unlit. The surface is asphalt, which the GIS inventory states, a harder, rougher surface than the acrylic most dedicated courts use. The lines sit on basketball courts, so expect to share with basketball rather than tennis. Raleigh Parks' sign-up guidelines apply (sign in or place a paddle, games to 11 and win by 2, all four players off at the end of each game), though with two courts and no lights the daylight is the likelier constraint. No fee is published for these courts.

faqs.q: Are there lights at Southgate Park?
faqs.a: No. Raleigh Parks marks this location No in the Lights column of its pickleball table. It is one of two unlit pickleball locations in the city, with Fred Fletcher Park.

faqs.q: What surface are the courts at Southgate Park?
faqs.a: Asphalt, according to the city's GIS court inventory. Southgate is the only one of the eleven Raleigh locations where that field is filled in; everywhere else it is empty, which is why every other Raleigh venue shows its surface as not verified.

slots.description: Tarboro Road Park sits close to downtown Raleigh on North Tarboro Street and offers two lit pickleball courts, painted onto the park's tennis courts. The department's pickleball page, its GIS court inventory and the commercial dataset this directory started from all give two. A community centre shares the park, and so does the Saint Monica Teen Center, each keeping its own published hours. It is one of the more central places to play in a city whose biggest pickleball sites are further out, and one of nine lit Raleigh locations. The courts belong to tennis as much as to pickleball, and with two of them a queue forms quickly.
slots.getting_there: 121 N. Tarboro Street, postcode 27610, just east of downtown. Raleigh Parks publishes no parking guidance for the courts. No restroom is recorded for the park itself in the city's amenities inventory, though the community centre and teen centre on the same site keep public hours. The park's page carries separate opening hours for the park, the community centre and the teen centre, and none of them states when the outdoor courts are available, so no court hours are published here.
slots.what_to_expect: Two lit courts over tennis lines. The lights run on a timer until 10 p.m. Raleigh Parks' rotation guidelines govern play: sign in or place your paddle, games singles or doubles to 11 points and win by 2, and all four players leave the court at the end of each game. Groups are asked to skip to the next fully open quadrant rather than break one up. The city does not state whether nets are provided, so bring one. It does not publish a surface material or a fee; the $3 session and $15 four-month pass are for indoor open play at its community centres, and the centre on this site is one of the thirteen that runs it.

faqs.q: Is Tarboro Road Park a good central option?
faqs.a: It is one of the closest verified pickleball locations to downtown Raleigh, and it is lit, so it works after work. It has two courts shared with tennis, so it is a convenient option rather than a spacious one.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are at Tarboro Road Park?
faqs.a: Two, and every record agrees: Raleigh Parks' pickleball page, its GIS court inventory and the commercial dataset this directory started from. They are pickleball lines on the park's tennis courts rather than dedicated courts.
